extracted.subtask_description: Writing and filing frontline wartime newspaper dispatches that combine official communiques, operational details, and eyewitness human-interest accounts while respecting military security and censorship rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military security limits on press dispatches / censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Ban on direct filing of press dispatches; dispatches to be sent by courier to Naples for censorship rather than being transmitted from the beachhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Route frontline reports through military/authorized censorship channels (e.g., couriering to censorship headquarters) and comply with commanders' decisions about filing. Balance the public's right to information with military security needs, as reflected in the quote that the public is "entitled to the fullest [information] consistent with military security."

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold operational dates and locations when required by security
rubrics_metrics.description: The announcement gave only bare details; the date is withheld because "the enemy does not know of the results of this attack" and "military security now permits announcement of the sinking."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish specific dates, times, or precise locations of sensitive operations when release could aid the enemy. If information is withheld for security, report that fact explicitly and attribute the reason to military authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official communiques as primary sources but note omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports rely on Gen. Douglas MacArthur’s communique and note when for the first time he omitted the Solomons heading or other routine items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat official communiques as authoritative sources for operational facts, but observe and report any conspicuous omissions or changes in format/content (these may signal operational security decisions or shifts in strategy). Attribute factual claims to the issuing communique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concrete operational details (tonnage, ship types, numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispatch lists specifics such as an 8,000-ton tanker beached, a 6,000-ton transport, three 1,500-ton cargo ships, totals of explosives (e.g., 221 tons), numbers of planes shot down, and numbers of vessels sunk or damaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measurable, concrete details (ship tonnage, number and type of aircraft, number of vessels sunk/damaged, numbers of casualties or rescued) when available and attributable; these lend precision and credibility. Where figures are uncertain, attribute them (e.g., "was listed in Gen. Douglas MacArthur’s communique").

rubrics_metrics.name: Include eyewitness and human-interest accounts with named sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The article incorporates first-person rescue narratives and named individuals (e.g., Lieut. (j.g.) Nathan G. Gordon, Vern Haugland, Father Anthony Cruysberg) to illustrate events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment operational reporting with eyewitness descriptions, personal quotes, and named sources to humanize the story and provide vivid detail. Identify speakers and their affiliations/roles, and corroborate where possible with official reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute uncertain claims and distinguish confirmed facts from reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases such as "the reports said," "the Army said," and noting that "supporting his statement... MacArthur omitted..." are used to indicate provenance and certainty levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly attribute information to its source (army, communique, eyewitness, correspondent). When information is incomplete or based on scattered reports, flag uncertainty and avoid presenting unconfirmed details as fact.
